title: Epigenetic and transcriptomic reprogramming in monocytes of severe COVID-19 patients reflects alterations in myeloid differentiation and the influence of inflammatory cytokines
authors: Godoy-Tena G; Barmada A; Morante-Palacios O; de la Calle-Fabregat C; Martins-Ferreira R; Ferreté-Bonastre AG; Ciudad L; Ruiz-Sanmartín A; Martínez-Gallo M; Ferrer R; Ruiz-Rodriguez JC; Rodríguez-Ubreva J; Vento-Tormo R; Ballestar E
one_liner_zh: 该研究分析重症COVID-19患者单核细胞的DNA甲基化与转录组变化，属于纯表观遗传和转录组学分析，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: COVID-19 manifests with a wide spectrum of clinical phenotypes, ranging from asymptomatic and mild to severe and critical. Severe and critical COVID-19 patients are characterized by marked changes in the myeloid compartment, especially monocytes. However, little is known about the epigenetic alterations that occur in these cells during hyperinflammatory responses in severe COVID-19 patients. In this study, we obtained the DNA methylome and transcriptome of peripheral blood monocytes from severe COVID-19 patients. DNA samples extracted from CD14+CD15-monocytes of 48 severe COVID-19 patients and 11 healthy controls were hybridized on MethylationEPIC BeadChip arrays. In parallel, single-cell transcriptomics of 10 severe COVID-19 patients were generated. CellPhoneDB was used to infer changes in the crosstalk between monocytes and other immune cell types. We observed DNA methylation changes in CpG sites associated with interferon-related genes and genes associated with antigen presentation, concordant with gene expression changes. These changes significantly overlapped with those occurring in bacterial sepsis, although specific DNA methylation alterations in genes specific to viral infection were also identified. We also found these alterations to comprise some of the DNA methylation changes occurring during myeloid differentiation and under the influence of inflammatory cytokines. A progression of DNA methylation alterations in relation to the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score was found to be related to interferon-related genes and T-helper 1 cell cytokine production. CellPhoneDB analysis of the single-cell transcriptomes of other immune cell types suggested the existence of altered crosstalk between monocytes and other cell types like NK cells and regulatory T cells. Our findings show the occurrence of an epigenetic and transcriptional reprogramming of peripheral blood monocytes, which could be associated with the release of aberrant immature monocytes, increased systemic levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines, and changes in immune cell crosstalk in these patients.
abstract_zh: COVID-19表现为广泛的临床表型谱，从无症状和轻度到重度和危重不等。重度和危重COVID-19患者的特征在于髓系区室（尤其是单核细胞）的显著变化。然而，关于这些细胞在重症COVID-19患者高炎症反应期间发生的表观遗传改变知之甚少。在本研究中，我们获取了重症COVID-19患者外周血单核细胞的DNA甲基化组和转录组。从48名重症COVID-19患者和11名健康对照者的CD14+CD15-单核细胞中提取的DNA样本，在MethylationEPIC BeadChip阵列上进行了杂交。同时，生成了10名重症COVID-19患者的单细胞转录组数据。使用CellPhoneDB推断单核细胞与其他免疫细胞类型之间串扰的变化。我们观察到与干扰素相关基因和抗原呈递相关基因相关的CpG位点发生DNA甲基化改变，这与基因表达变化一致。这些改变与细菌性脓毒症中发生的改变显著重叠，尽管也识别出病毒特异性感染基因的特异性DNA甲基化改变。我们还发现这些改变包含髓系分化过程中及炎症细胞因子影响下发生的一些DNA甲基化变化。发现与序贯器官衰竭评估（SOFA）评分相关的DNA甲基化改变进展与干扰素相关基因和T辅助1细胞细胞因子产生有关。对其他免疫细胞类型单细胞转录组的CellPhoneDB分析提示，单核细胞与自然杀伤细胞和调节性T细胞等其他细胞类型之间存在改变的串扰。我们的发现表明，外周血单核细胞发生了表观遗传和转录重编程，这可能与这些患者中异常未成熟单核细胞的释放、促炎细胞因子全身水平升高以及免疫细胞串扰的变化有关。
